title: How Integrated Data Improves Provider Directory Management
summary: Learn how provider data integration improves provider directory accuracy, reduces administrative work, and supports compliance across healthcare.
body_text: KEY TAKEAWAYS ​Integrated provider directory management helps organizations create a single, reliable source of provider data. ​Connected provider data reduces duplicate records, outdated information, and manual reconciliation. ​Strong provider data interoperability supports faster updates across credentialing, enrollment, directory, and claims workflows. ​Better provider data governance improves provider data quality, compliance readiness, and operational performance. ​Provider directory integration best practices help organizations create scalable processes that support long-term provider lifecycle needs. Understanding integrated provider directory management​​ ‍ Integrated provider directory management is the practice of connecting provider information across credentialing, enrollment, directory, claims, and other operational systems so healthcare organizations can maintain one accurate, current source of provider data. ​When organizations rely on disconnected systems, provider records become harder to manage, harder to trust, and harder to keep compliant. With provider data integration, teams can improve provider directory accuracy, reduce administrative work, and support better experiences for patients, providers, and staff. ​Why provider directory management depends on integrated data ​Healthcare organizations manage provider information across many systems, including credentialing platforms, enrollment applications, electronic health records (EHRs), claims systems, customer relationship management (CRM) tools, and provider directories. Each system may serve a different purpose, but the data often overlaps. If those systems are not connected, a single provider update can create multiple versions of the truth. ​That is why integrated provider data matters. Address changes, specialty updates, licensure changes, network participation updates, and credentialing status changes need to move across systems quickly and consistently. When they do not, organizations face directory inaccuracies, delayed workflows, and avoidable administrative burden. ​Effective provider directory management depends on provider directory integration that allows information to move across the organization. This shifts directory work from reactive cleanup to proactive provider lifecycle management, connecting onboarding, credentialing, enrollment, network management, and ongoing data maintenance. ​ ​The hidden costs of disconnected provider data ​Duplicate records ​Duplicate records make it difficult to know which provider information is correct. They also increase manual work for credentialing, enrollment, payer relations, and directory teams. Strong provider master data management helps reduce duplication by creating a governed source of truth that supports multiple workflows. ​Outdated provider information ​Provider information changes frequently. Without reliable provider data synchronization, a directory may continue to display old phone numbers, addresses, specialties, affiliations, or network status. A 2024 study from The American Journal of Managed Care found that 40.3% of previously identified inaccurate provider listings still contained errors more than a year later, despite federal requirements for regular verification and updates. These errors can spread quickly when updates are entered in one system but not shared with others. ​A 2024 study found that 40.3% of previously identified inaccurate provider listings still contained errors more than a year later. ​Administrative inefficiencies ​Disconnected data forces staff to compare records, update spreadsheets, reenter information, and resolve inconsistencies manually. Provider data integration reduces this repetitive work by helping systems exchange information more efficiently and consistently. ​​Poor patient experience ​Patients rely on provider directories to find care, confirm network participation, and schedule appointments. Inaccurate provider information can lead to delays, frustration, and unexpected costs. Organizations asking how to improve provider directory accuracy should start by connecting the systems that create, verify, update, and publish provider data. ​Compliance risks ​Federal expectations have increased the pressure on organizations to maintain accurate provider directory information. CMS provides guidance on No Surprises Act provider requirements including provider directory obligations, and offers broader No Surprises Act resources for providers, facilities, health plans, and issuers. Integrated data helps organizations maintain more consistent records, document updates, and support audit readiness. ​​What does integrated provider data mean? ​Integrated provider data management means provider information is centralized, standardized, governed, and shared across systems. Instead of maintaining separate records in separate platforms, organizations create a connected data environment that supports the full provider lifecycle. ​Integrated provider data supports: ​A single source of truth ​Provider data interoperability ​Real-time or near-real-time provider data synchronization ​Provider lifecycle connectivity ​Strong provider data governance ​Higher provider data quality ​This approach helps organizations manage provider information from initial onboarding and credentialing through enrollment, directory updates, network management, claims support, and ongoing maintenance. ​How integrated data improves provider directory management Creates a single source of truth ​A single source of truth gives teams one reliable place to manage provider information. This improves reporting, reduces confusion, and helps departments work from the same data. For payer organizations managing complex networks, V12 Enterprise by HealthStream supports provider network management and centralized provider data operations across the provider lifecycle. ​Connects credentialing, enrollment, and directory management ​Connecting credentialing and provider directories is essential because credentialing and enrollment teams often collect and verify provider information before it appears in a directory. When these workflows are disconnected, verified data may not flow into the systems that patients, members, and internal teams use. ​ CredentialStream supports credentialing, enrollment, and privileging workflows, helping organizations manage provider information more consistently as part of a broader provider data management strategy. ​Synchronizes updates across systems ​Application programming interfaces (APIs) help systems exchange provider information automatically, reducing the need for manual updates. With stronger provider directory interoperability, changes can move across credentialing platforms, enrollment systems, directories, claims systems, and other applications with less delay. ​This is one of the clearest examples of how integrated data improves provider directories. Automated updates help reduce directory drift, improve consistency, and support more dependable provider information across the organization. ​​Improves provider data quality ​Strong provider data quality depends on validation, deduplication, standardization, and continuous monitoring. Integrated systems make these activities easier because teams can identify inconsistencies earlier and correct them before they spread. ​Organizations can also use authoritative sources such as the National Plan and Provider Enumeration System NPI Registry to support provider identification and verification. The Council for Affordable Quality Healthcare’s provider directory accuracy issue brief also highlights why directory accuracy remains a persistent healthcare challenge. ​Strengthens compliance ​Integrated data supports compliance by making provider information easier to maintain, verify, and audit. When data is centralized and governed, organizations can better document changes, track updates, and respond to regulatory expectations. ​Compliance also depends on repeatable processes. By using provider directory management best practices, organizations can reduce inconsistencies, improve oversight, and create a stronger foundation for long-term directory accuracy. ​The role of APIs and healthcare interoperability ​Modern provider data integration depends on APIs and interoperability standards that help systems exchange information securely and efficiently. This may include EHR integrations, credentialing platforms, provider enrollment systems, claims systems, CRM tools, and directory management applications. ​The Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology explains the importance of health IT interoperability , and its API resource guide provides information related to API standards and certification. For provider directory operations, interoperability is not just a technical goal. It is a strategic requirement for improving visibility, reducing rework, and creating more reliable provider data across the enterprise. ​Organizations evaluating broader credentialing and provider data needs can also review HealthStream Credentialing Solutions , which includes resources for credentialing, enrollment, privileging, and related provider data workflows. ​Benefits for different healthcare organizations ​Health plans ​Provider data integration for health plans supports network adequacy, directory accuracy, member satisfaction, and compliance readiness. Integrated data can help payer teams manage provider networks more efficiently and reduce errors that affect members. Health plans can explore healthcare software for payers for payer-focused resources related to provider network management and operational performance. ​Hospitals and health systems ​Hospitals and health systems depend on accurate provider information for referrals, scheduling, credentialing, privileging, and enterprise provider management. Connected provider data helps reduce siloed information across departments and facilities, making it easier to maintain consistent records and support operational decisions. ​Large medical groups ​Large medical groups often manage providers across multiple locations, specialties, and payer relationships. Integrated provider data supports growth by standardizing workflows, improving visibility, and reducing variation across locations. ​Best practices for building an integrated provider data strategy ​The benefits of integrated provider directory management depend on a practical, well-governed strategy. Organizations should: ​Centralize provider data ​Eliminate duplicate systems where possible ​Establish clear provider data governance ​Automate validation processes ​Connect systems through APIs ​Monitor provider data quality continuously ​Standardize workflows across departments ​These provider directory integration best practices help organizations improve accuracy while building more scalable provider operations. Related resources such as Network by HealthStream can support organizations focused on provider data management, network operations, and provider lifecycle workflows. ​Measuring success: KPIs for provider directory management ​Organizations can measure the success of an integrated provider directory management strategy using key performance indicators such as: ​Directory accuracy rate ​Time to update provider records ​Duplicate record reduction ​Compliance audit findings ​Provider attestation completion ​Patient complaints related to provider information ​Claim denial reduction ​These metrics help leaders connect data quality to operational value. They also show how reducing provider directory errors with integration can improve compliance readiness, administrative efficiency, and the patient experience. ​Frequently asked questions ​What is integrated provider directory management? ​Integrated provider directory management connects provider data across systems so organizations can maintain accurate, consistent, and current provider directory information. ​Why is integrated provider data important? ​Integrated provider data reduces silos, improves accuracy, and supports better provider operations across the full lifecycle. ​How does provider data integration improve directory accuracy? ​Provider data integration synchronizes updates, reduces duplicate records, standardizes information, and helps prevent conflicting data across systems. ​What systems should connect to a provider directory? ​Credentialing, enrollment, EHR, claims, CRM, provider network, and directory management systems should connect whenever possible. ​What are the benefits of real-time provider data synchronization? ​Real-time provider data synchronization helps organizations update records faster, reduce directory drift, and maintain more current provider information. ​How do APIs improve provider directory management? ​APIs enable automated information exchange, supporting stronger provider data interoperability and more efficient directory management.

title: Introducing the Thndr Zakat Calculator
body_text: Fulfill Your Financial Obligation without the guesswork Built from the questions, conversations, and needs we heard across our community, we’re excited to introduce the Thndr Zakat Calculator. This Calculator has been reviewed and approved by Dr. Magdy Ashour, Former Scientific Advisor to the Grand Mufti of Egypt. Last Ramadan, we noticed something important. Zakat questions kept coming up from our users. Not just as a general question, but as a real point of confusion: How do I calculate Zakat on stocks? Do savings products count? What about gold funds? What if my money is spread across multiple assets? As more people began building wealth across different Thndr products, one thing became clear: calculating Zakat accurately can get complicated, and at times, overwhelming. So we listened. And we built a simpler way to do it. At Thndr, we believe managing your finances should feel simple, and that includes fulfilling your religious obligations with confidence. That’s why we asked ourselves: what if Zakat calculation could be done easily, directly inside the app? What is the Zakat Calculator? The Zakat Calculator is a tool embedded within the Thndr app in My Hub that helps you calculate your Zakat based on Islamic principles. The best part? It automatically pre-fills your Thndr portfolio data, so you’re already halfway there before you even start. How does it work? Step 1: Open the Calculator The calculator calculates based on the Hijri year by default. But if you are following the Gregorian year in your Zakat, just choose it, and we’ve got you covered. The calculator shows you the current Nisab threshold (the minimum wealth required for Zakat) based on the latest gold price. This assumes that your reached the Nisab (your Hawl started) exactly one year ago. Start your Hawl on a different date? You can customize this! Tap on today’s date to select when your wealth crossed the threshold. This also allows you to calculate Zakat for any past year, not just the current one. Your Thndr wallet balance, Saving Clouds balance, and stock portfolio are already pre-filled for you to make your experience easier. You’ll just need to add assets you own outside Thndr. Step 2: Add Your Assets & Liabilities Enter your wealth across 8 categories, and don’t worry, your Thndr assets are already prefilled: Cash & Balances: Bank accounts, savings, physical cash Investments: Stocks & Mutual Funds Bank CDs: Certificates of deposit Gold: Coins, bars, or jewelry Silver: Coins, bars, or jewelry Real Estate: Properties you own Lendings: Money you’ve lent to others Business Assets: Inventory, receivables, business cash Debts: Money you owe (this reduces your Zakat amount) Purpose-based Calculation Different assets have different Zakat rules depending on their purpose. Be aware to enter the purpose for each investment, Thndr assets and external assets, in the calculator. The calculator guides you through the right treatment for each asset type. Step 3: Get Your Result Tap “Calculate Zakat” and instantly see your Zakat amount with a full breakdown. If your wealth is below the Nisab threshold, we’ll let you know that you’re not obligated to pay Zakat this year. Features you’ll love Custom Nisab Date — Set the exact date when your wealth first reached Nisab to calculate Zakat for any year — past or present. Smart Pre-filling: Your Thndr investment wallet, Clouds savings, and complete stock portfolio are automatically imported. Just add assets held outside Thndr. Purpose-Based Calculation: Different assets have different Zakat rules depending on their purpose. The calculator guides you through the right treatment for each asset type. Hijri or Gregorian Year: Choose to calculate based on the Islamic lunar year (2.5% rate) or the Gregorian year (2.577% rate). The preferred basis for calculation is the Hijri year. However, if someone needs to calculate using the Gregorian year, it is permissible. Quick Facts Nisab Basis: 85 grams of 21K gold Zakat Rate: 2.5% (Hijri) or 2.577% (Georgian) Hawl Requirement: Your wealth must stay above Nisab for one full continuous year Ready to calculate your Zakat? Open the Thndr app and find the Zakat Calculator to get started. It’s the easiest way to fulfill your obligation while keeping all your financial data in one place. For more details on how the amount is calculated, please visit the Zakat Calculator Support page . Have Questions? If you need any assistance, our in-app support team is ready to help. Just reach out, and we’ll guide you every step of the way !

title: Cadiz and RIC Energy Sign MOU to Advance Solar / Hydrogen Development at Cadiz Ranch
summary: Cadiz and RIC Energy Sign MOU to Advance Solar / Hydrogen Development at Cadiz Ranch
body_text: MOU expands companies’ green hydrogen collaboration by adding on-site solar generation and advancing hydrogen infrastructure planning in California’s Mojave Desert. LOS ANGELES, Calif. — Cadiz, Inc. (NASDAQ: CDZI, CDZIP) (“Cadiz”) and RIC Energy (“RIC”) today announced they have entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (“MOU”) to develop on-site solar facilities that will accelerate the transition of Cadiz’s agricultural operations to clean, renewable energy while expanding the companies’ collaboration on green hydrogen development. The MOU also establishes a framework to evaluate the feasibility of siting, permitting and constructing dedicated hydrogen transportation infrastructure—including hydrogen pipelines and other transport solutions—utilizing Cadiz’s existing 220-mile Northern Pipeline corridor and other rights-of-way to support future delivery of hydrogen to regional markets and other off-site customers. The MOU announced today expands a strategic collaboration launched by the two companies in October 2024 to develop green hydrogen production at Cadiz Ranch by adding on-site solar generation as the first phase of an integrated renewable energy platform. Under the MOU, RIC will develop solar facilities to power Cadiz’s agricultural operations while the companies continue advancing hydrogen production facilities and related infrastructure at Cadiz Ranch. Together, the solar and hydrogen projects are intended to provide reliable, cost-effective, low-carbon energy resources for Cadiz’s agricultural operations, the Mojave Groundwater Bank and other regional water supply projects in San Bernardino County. “Our partnership with RIC demonstrates how renewable energy and low-carbon fuels can power the next generation of water infrastructure,” said Susan Kennedy, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Cadiz. “Last year we transitioned away from diesel and are advancing clean energy solutions for future operations. This MOU enables the next step—powering those operations with on-site solar generation while advancing green hydrogen as a future fuel source for the Mojave Groundwater Bank and other regional water infrastructure. Together, we’re building an integrated clean energy platform that leverages the abundant solar, water and land resources at Cadiz Ranch.” “The opportunity extends well beyond a traditional solar and battery energy storage project,” said Jonathan Rappe, CEO of RIC Energy North America. “Together we are designing an integrated renewable energy platform that can evolve alongside the hydrogen economy and support one of California’s most important water infrastructure developments.” Under the MOU, the companies will negotiate a definitive power purchase agreement (PPA) for electricity generated by new on-site solar facilities while jointly planning infrastructure to support future hydrogen production, storage and delivery. The framework also provides for coordinated evaluation of electrical infrastructure, transmission facilities and other systems needed to integrate solar generation with future hydrogen production at Cadiz Ranch. As part of this effort, the companies will evaluate the feasibility of siting, permitting and constructing dedicated hydrogen transportation infrastructure, including hydrogen pipelines and other transport solutions, within Cadiz’s existing 220-mile Northern Pipeline corridor and other rights-of-way to support delivery of hydrogen to regional markets and other off-site customers. The infrastructure planning effort is intended to preserve practical, cost-effective pathways for future hydrogen transportation while supporting development of regional water and energy infrastructure projects throughout San Bernardino County. The MOU follows two recent milestones that position the Company to commence construction of the Mojave Groundwater Bank upon completion of project financing. Earlier this month, the U.S. Bureau of Land Management approved a new right-of-way grant for Cadiz’s 220-mile Northern Pipeline, allowing the Company to convert the pipeline from natural gas service to water conveyance. Earlier this year, San Bernardino County and Fenner Gap Mutual Water Company formed the San Bernardino Water and Power Authority to support the financing and development of regional water and energy infrastructure projects throughout San Bernardino County. About Cadiz, Inc. Cadiz, Inc. (NASDAQ: CDZI) is a water solutions and natural resources company developing long-term water supply, storage, conveyance and treatment solutions for communities, businesses, farmers and public agencies across the Southwest. Founded in 1983, Cadiz owns approximately 45,000 acres of land and 220 miles of pipeline assets in California’s Mojave Desert. Its assets include Cadiz Ranch, the largest agricultural operation in San Bernardino County; the Mojave Groundwater Bank, one of the largest new water supply and groundwater storage projects in the Lower Colorado River Basin; and ATEC Water Systems, which provides specialized groundwater treatment technology throughout the western United States. For more information, visit https://www.cadizinc.com . Founded in Spain in 2005, RIC Energy expanded into North America in 2010 and has since successfully deployed gigawatts of distributed and utility-scale solar and energy storage, and green hydrogen projects.
